record.abstract: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching. This method integrates novel retrieval mechanisms, including LLM-based, vector-based, graph traversal-based, and hybrid techniques with advanced reranking schemes to extract the most relevant subgraphs from large external KGs. Our approach achieves superior results without requiring re-training, as evidenced by improvements of 39.79% in precision and 30.56% in F1 score over LLM-based state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods (e.g., Jellyfish-8B) on the MIMIC dataset, and enhancements of 69.20% in precision and 21.99% in F1 score over pre-trained language model (PLM)-based SOTA methods (e.g., SMAT) on the Synthea dataset. Additionally, KG-RAG4SM scales effectively across KGs from commonsense KGs to domain-specific ones, while its instruction-tuning knowledge exclusion component ensures truthful performance in end-to-end schema matching tasks despite the suboptimal relevance of KG context. Our empirical analysis and case studies from real-world scenarios show that the hallucination problem in LLMs for schema matching is well mitigated by our solution.

record.abstract: Hardware fault injection attacks threaten machine learning systems, yet their impact on reinforcement learning (RL) has received little attention despite the use of RL in safety-critical applications. This paper presents a security analysis of Q-Learning implementations under voltage and clock glitching attacks on a ChipWhisperer platform, evaluating five variants: Standard, Robust, Resilient, Linear, and Deep Q-Learning. In standard Q-Table implementations, faults corrupt reward computation, action selection, and Q-value updates during learning, and change the selected action during inference. Robust Q-Learning does not prevent these attacks: NaN and infinite values injected during learning persist in the Q-table, and its greedy policy uses the same code as standard Q-Learning. This paper also evaluates a Resilient Q-Learning variant that applies triple modular redundancy with majority voting. It corrects corruption of a single Q-table copy, but inputs shared by the copies, such as the reward, and the voting code itself remain outside its protection. The analysis extends to Linear and Deep Q-Learning, where faults corrupt stored weights during learning and change actions during inference. Moving beyond benchmark environments, this work evaluates an online traffic light controller in a microscopic traffic simulator, where a single injected infinite value degrades accumulated vehicle waiting time by 148x while corrupting under 4% of the Q-table, and where triple modular redundancy corrected the faults injected in our tests, although glitching could still halt the device. Altogether, this work provides a basis for understanding and securing RL deployments against fault injection attacks.

record.abstract: In vehicular integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, each service-provider vehicle uses a limited power budget to serve multiple sensing targets and communication receivers. Maximizing the communication sum-rate subject to sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints is nonconvex, and iterative optimization is costly to rerun for every network layout. This paper proposes a graph neural network (GNN)-based power allocation algorithm, termed GNN-ISAC. Concretely, GNN-ISAC addresses the aforementioned problem by considering two distinct edge types in the graph representation, one capturing the inter-provider interference, the other representing the intra-provider power-budget sharing. GNN-ISAC is trained without labels using a sensing-penalized sum-rate loss. We also adapt the weighted mean-square error minimization (WMMSE) algorithm to this problem by introducing a sensing-power reservation step. Simulation results show that GNN-ISAC achieves communication sum-rates close to WMMSE with low sensing-link violation rates and much less computation. It also outperforms an existing heterogeneous GNN and a channel-blind baseline, and generalizes to larger networks without retraining.

record.abstract: Combinations of the most recent CMB, BAO, and SNeIa datasets, when analyzed using the Chevallier–Polarski–Linder (CPL) parametrization, w ( a ) = w 0 + ( 1 − a ) w a , exclude Λ CDM at ≳ 3 σ in favor of a dark energy equation of state (EoS) parameter that crosses the phantom divide. We confirm this behavior and show that it persists when Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument BAO data are replaced by SH0ES H 0 measurements, despite the known tension between these probes in the presence of CMB data. In both cases, the constraints favor a transition from an early-time phantomlike phase to a late-time quintessencelike phase, with the crossing occurring at different redshifts depending on the dataset combination. The probability that a phantom divide line (PDL) crossing does not occur within the expansion history is excluded at significance levels ranging between 3.1 σ – 5.2 σ . To investigate whether the apparent PDL crossing is a genuine feature preferred by the data or an artifact of the linear form of the CPL parametrization, we isolate the PDL crossing feature by introducing two modified versions of CPL that explicitly forbid it: CPL > a c and CPL < a c . These models are physically motivated in that they phenomenologically capture the behavior of thawing and freezing scalar field scenarios. While previous studies have primarily considered thawing quintessence as a noncrossing alternative, we find that a freezing phantomlike model is the only one capable of performing comparably to CPL—and only in a few cases. Nevertheless, across all dataset combinations considered, the standard CPL model consistently provides the best fit, strongly indicating that the data genuinely favor a PDL crossing.

record.abstract: Locating and fixing software faults is challenging. Traditional Spectrum-Based Fault Localization (SBFL) uses test coverage and failure data but often suffers from low accuracy due to a lack of semantic understanding of code. Deep-learning approaches can improve localization, but require extensive training data and computational resources. Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative with stronger code reasoning capabilities. However, existing LLM-based fault localization techniques still struggle at the repository level due to large context windows and positional bias, in which important debugging signals may be buried in large contexts. In this work, we introduce LLM4FL , a multi-LLM-agent-based fault localization technique designed to address these challenges. LLM4FL uses three specialized agents. The Context Extraction Agent divides and prioritizes covered methods into token-fitting groups using an order-aware strategy based on Ochiai suspiciousness scores. The Debugger Agent navigates the repository through graph-based retrieval to generate failure reasoning and rank suspicious methods. The Reviewer Agent then re-evaluates and re-ranks the results through iterative self-refinement and verbal reasoning. Evaluated on Defects4J, LLM4FL improves Top-1 accuracy over prior LLM-based approaches, including AutoFL and SoapFL , by 14.5% and 4.58%, respectively. Our ablation study further highlights the importance of LLM4FL's design choices, with failure reason generation improving Top-1 performance by 12.5% and order-aware division substantially improving localization accuracy by 18.07%.

record.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.

record.abstract: Tidal Love numbers of black holes, zero in classical general relativity for Kerr black holes in vacuum, become non-vanishing in the presence of exotic matter or in alternative theories of gravity, making them a powerful probe of fundamental physics. The gravitational-wave event GW250114, observed with an exceptionally high signal-to-noise ratio, provides a unique opportunity to test this prediction. By analyzing this event, we conclude that the data are consistent with the binary black hole hypothesis, and we place a 90% upper limit on the effective tidal deformability of Λ ̃ < 34.8 . These bounds imply that any matter distribution surrounding each black hole individually must contribute less than ∼ 7 × 10 − 3 of its mass, and they rule out some models of boson stars. Our findings provide the strongest observational constraints yet on black hole tidal deformability and show that the data remain fully consistent with the Kerr black hole prediction of vanishing tidal Love numbers.

record.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate discovery by reasoning across the ever-expanding landscape of scientific knowledge. Yet, as the reservoir of knowledge grows, the challenge is no longer access to information but rather the ability to connect it in meaningful, domain-spanning ways. In materials science, where discoveries and new hypotheses emerge from bridging insights across disciplines and demand the integration of concepts from molecular chemistry to mechanical performance, this challenge is especially acute. Neither human researchers nor single-agent LLMs can contend with this torrent of information, with the latter often producing brittle reasoning and hallucinations. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a multiagent framework guided by large-scale knowledge graphs to address the urgent challenge of finding sustainable substitutes for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a class of synthetic chemicals widely used in industrial and consumer applications that are the subject of increasing regulatory scrutiny due to concerns raised in scientific literature and evolving policy efforts to ban certain PFAS compounds. Agents in the framework specialize in problem decomposition, evidence retrieval, design parameter extraction, and graph traversal, uncovering latent connections across distinct pockets of scientific knowledge that support downstream hypothesis generation for PFAS-free materials. Our ablation studies show that the full multiagent pipeline outperforms single-shot prompting, underscoring the value of distributed specialization and relational reasoning. We show that by tailoring graph traversal strategies, the system can alternate between exploitative searches that focus hypothesis generation on domain-critical outcomes and exploratory searches that surface emergent cross-connections in the broader network. Shown through the exemplar of biomedical tubing, the framework generates sustainable material alternatives to PFAS-based tubing that balance tribological performance, thermal stability, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility. This work establishes a framework that combines knowledge graphs with multiagent reasoning to expand the materials design space and reveal interdisciplinary connections. We showcase several initial PFAS-free design candidates to demonstrate the approach.

record.abstract: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)-component Schrödinger's cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.

Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. record.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing clients’ raw data, but parameter exchange can impose substantial communication costs and usually requires compatible model architectures. Federated distillation (FD) instead transfers predictive or intermediate knowledge through knowledge distillation (KD), which can support heterogeneous models and reduce communication in suitable settings. These benefits are not automatic: their magnitude depends on the transmitted knowledge, reference data, communication schedule, and threat model. This survey provides a challenge-centered synthesis of FD. We first formalize a representative public-data, response-based FD protocol and then organize existing methods by the FL challenges they address, including data, system, and model heterogeneity, client drift, catastrophic forgetting, communication cost, and privacy risk. We further review applications in industrial engineering, computer vision, natural language processing, and healthcare, including recent federated adaptation of large language models. Finally, we identify five research priorities: richer transferred knowledge, joint treatment of interacting forms of heterogeneity, communication-aware distillation, threat-model-driven privacy protection, and standardized theory, benchmarks, and evaluation.

record.abstract: We compute the galaxy power spectrum at two-loop order in cosmological perturbation theory (effective field theory, EFT). We derive galaxy bias operators through the fifth order and obtain two-loop renormalization conditions for their bias coefficients. We also derive the relevant higher-derivative and stochastic contributions, and implement IR resummation using . We obtain complete dark-matter and galaxy renormalization conditions for the higher-derivative operators at the power spectrum, bispectrum, and trispectrum level. Having identified the redundant operators, we find that the two-loop galaxy-galaxy and galaxy-matter power spectra require 28 additional bias, higher derivative, and stochastic parameters per galaxy sample relative to the one-loop model. record.abstract: String breaking is at the core of hadronization models of relevance to particle colliders. Yet, studies of string-breaking dynamics rooted in quantum chromodynamics remain fundamentally challenging. Tensor networks enable sign-problem-free studies of static and dynamical properties of lattice gauge theories. In this work, we develop and apply a tensor-network toolkit based on the loop-string-hadron formulation of an SU(2) lattice gauge theory in 1+1 dimensions with dynamical fermions. We apply this toolkit to study static and dynamical aspects of strings and their breaking in this theory. The simple, gauge-invariant, and local structure of the loop-string-hadron states and constraints removes the need to impose non-Abelian constraints in the algorithm, and allows for a systematic computation of observables at increasingly large bosonic cutoffs, and toward the infinite-volume and continuum limits. Our study of static strings yields a determination of the string tension in the continuum and thermodynamic limits. Our study of dynamical string breaking, performed at a fixed lattice spacing and system size, illuminates underlying processes at play during the quench dynamics of a string. The loop, string, and hadron description offers a systematic and intuitive way to diagnose these processes, including string expansion and contraction, endpoint splitting and particle shower, chain scattering events, and inelastic processes resulting from string dissociation and recombination, and particle production. We relate these processes to several features of the dynamics, such as energy transport, entanglement-entropy production, and correlation spreading. This work opens the way to future tensor-network studies of string breaking and particle production in increasingly complex lattice gauge theories.

record.abstract: Contextual anomaly detection in tabular data aims to identify objects whose behavior is unexpected under their contextual conditions. In data-engineering pipelines, this task screens table rows whose measurements violate context-dependent integrity relationships. Most existing approaches rely on either shallow conditional models with limited distributional expressiveness or localized estimators that require per-context modeling, making it difficult to capture complex conditional relationships and scale to high-dimensional settings. We propose Flow-CAD, a new framework for contextual anomaly detection based on Flow Matching. Flow-CAD learns a single global and amortized conditional generative model that flexibly represents behavioral distributions conditioned on context, without assuming simple parametric forms or retraining local models. To enable robust and interpretable anomaly scoring, we introduce a scale-normalized and truncated residual energy derived from the learned conditional flow, which stabilizes anomaly scores, mitigates domination by extreme deviations, and supports feature-wise attribution. We further provide theoretical insights showing that the proposed residual-based anomaly score is stable under velocity estimation error, and that its Monte Carlo estimator satisfies concentration bounds. Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets with 13 competitors demonstrate that Flow-CAD has the best average rank for PR AUC, ROC AUC, and P@n, highlighting its effectiveness and practicality for contextual anomaly detection in tabular data. We provide the source code at https://github.com/ZhongLIFR/FlowCAD.

record.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges and collapses in correlated electron systems remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. As a recently discovered member of the high temperature superconductor family, bilayer nickelates provide a new opportunity for examining this problem. Their pronounced sensitivity to oxygen stoichiometry, while posing challenges for stabilizing superconductivity, simultaneously offers an effective control parameter for tuning electronic phases. Here we report a superconducting half-dome in compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films as a function of continuous tuning of oxygen stoichiometry. Starting from an optimally superconducting state, increasing oxygen stoichiometry gradually suppresses superconductivity toward a metallic phase, whereas decreasing oxygen stoichiometry drives a granular superconductor-to-insulator transition while leaving the superconducting onset intact. This half-dome structure is consistent with the contrasting roles played by interstitial oxygen versus oxygen vacancies—namely, the dominance of doping versus scattering. Notably, the half-dome emerges consistently across samples with different rare-earth combinations, with or without alkaline-earth doping, revealing a general feature of the bilayer nickelate phase diagram and informing opportunities for further enhancing superconductivity.

record.abstract: As cyber threats grow in complexity and frequency, institutions face increasing challenges in safeguarding sensitive data and ensuring the integrity of their network infrastructures. Traditional security mechanisms often struggle to keep pace with rapidly evolving attack vectors. This paper presents a conceptual framework for AI-augmented threat detection in institutional networks, leveraging layered data aggregation and pattern recognition techniques to enhance the accuracy and speed of threat identification. The proposed model integrates artificial intelligence (AI) with multi-layered network monitoring systems to collect, analyze, and interpret real-time data from various sources including firewalls, endpoints, and intrusion detection systems (IDS). The framework is designed around three core components: data aggregation, feature extraction, and intelligent pattern recognition. Data aggregation collects and consolidates log files and event streams from disparate network components into a centralized repository. Feature extraction applies preprocessing algorithms to identify critical attributes such as access anomalies, packet irregularities, and login behavior deviations. The pattern recognition layer utilizes machine learning and deep learning models to detect deviations from established behavioral baselines and predict potential threats, including zeroday attacks and insider threats. A key innovation of this framework is the use of contextual layering, where data is categorized and analyzed at different abstraction levels—user, application, and system—allowing for a more nuanced understanding of threat dynamics. This layered approach supports adaptive learning, enabling the AI models to refine detection capabilities over time through continuous feedback. Furthermore, the system can generate alerts and automated responses in real time, improving the institution’s resilience against cyber intrusions. The paper discusses implementation considerations, challenges in training AI models with diverse datasets, and the importance of explainable AI (XAI) for transparency in threat detection decisions. By offering a scalable and intelligent approach, the framework aims to strengthen cybersecurity in academic and enterprise environments. record.abstract: A double-transmon coupler (DTC) enables a fast, high-fidelity CZ gate between two highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits. record.abstract: The unitary cluster Jastrow (UCJ) ansatz and its variant known as local UCJ (LUCJ) are promising choices for variational quantum algorithms for chemistry due to their combination of physical motivation and hardware efficiency. The parameters of these ansatzes can be initialized from the output of a coupled cluster, singles and doubles (CCSD) calculation performed on a classical computer. However, truncating the number of repetitions of the ansatz, as well as discarding interactions to accommodate the connectivity constraints of near-term quantum processors, degrade the approximation to CCSD and the resulting energy accuracy. In this work, we propose two methods to improve the parameter initialization. The first method, which is applicable to both expectation value- and sample-based algorithms, uses compressed double factorization of the CCSD amplitudes to improve or recover the CCSD approximation. The second method, which is applicable to sample-based algorithms, uses approximate tensor network simulation to improve the quality of samples produced by the ansatz circuit. Both methods perform classical preprocessing to construct the initial circuit parameters and can be followed by parameter optimization using quantum measurements, although we do not perform such optimization in this work. We validate our methods using exact state vector simulation on systems of up to 52 qubits, as well as experiments on superconducting quantum processors using up to 65 qubits. Our results indicate that our methods can significantly improve the output of both expectation value- and sample-based quantum algorithms.

record.abstract: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin s = 1 ) and `colorful' ( s ≥ 2 ) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as n in system size n ), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the s = 1 chain exhibits U ( 1 ) spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the s ≥ 2 chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh \cite{movassagh2017entanglement}, while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The n entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension e Ω ( n ) ; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.

record.abstract: Digital Twins are evolving from passive virtual representations into closed-loop systems that continuously synchronize with physical assets and drive real-time decisions. Yet predictive modeling, machine learning (ML), uncertainty quantification (UQ), and decision-making have been studied as separate capabilities, leaving limited understanding of their integration and maintenance during online operation. This narrative review, scoped by the functional requirements of real-time decision-making rather than by Digital Twin terminology alone, examines how such decisions are generated and sustained in engineering Digital Twins. We first examine foundational decision-making architectures and representative engineering applications, followed by methods that address their limitations across the decision loop. We identify optimization-based, policy-based, and knowledge-based approaches as the major pathways from virtual representation to action. Across them, ML plays three roles in decision-making: enabling efficient surrogate modeling, transforming heterogeneous physical feedback into decision-relevant information, and accelerating or directly generating decisions. UQ supports uncertainty-aware decisions and model adaptation, while continual validation, drift detection, and adaptation help maintain reliable operation as the physical system evolves. Together, these findings underscore the need for a shift from a model-centric to a system-centric perspective on Digital Twins, where its performance depends on the interactions with sensing, state estimation, computation, decision-making, and adaptation rather than on their standalone performance. Therefore, future research should shift from isolated algorithm development toward system-level co-design, scalable decision-making, and approaches to design, and data-efficient continual adaptation and validation for AI-enabled autonomous systems.

record.abstract: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian power system collapsed after a rapid voltage rise that led to widespread generation disconnections and loss of synchronism. For each candidate event, the method computes the voltage at every overvoltage relay over the relay time window from a dynamic model of the network, its controls, and its relays. It predicts which relays trip after a first trip, identifies assets whose relay or measurement data are insufficient for a safety conclusion, and, when one exists, computes a minimum-cost fast reactive power action that keeps all relay voltages below their settings. record.abstract: We analyze the closed and autonomous interaction between quantum matter and classical objects through a general effective channel for hybrid dynamics, subject to the fundamental constraint that no quantum correlations can be generated between the classical and quantum sectors from any initially separable state. We demonstrate that, within this hybrid framework, imposing an additive conserved observable ⟨OQC ⟩ = ⟨OQ⟩ + ⟨OC ⟩ strictly forbids a classical system from altering the local observable ⟨OQ⟩ of its quantum counterpart. Applying this no-go theorem to gravity, under the assumption of such hybrid dynamics, we show that if global momentum is conserved, a strictly classical gravitational field cannot induce momentum transfers in a quantum system. In contrast, a quantum gravitational field naturally facilitates such back-action. Drawing upon the fundamental relationship between conservation laws and the quantum properties of objects, our analysis provides a novel perspective for interpreting existing experimental observations, such as free fall, as potential indicators of the non-classicality of gravity.

record.abstract: Observation of the quantum Mpemba effect has spurred much interest in its enabling conditions and its relation to the classical counterpart. Here, we consider weakly open many-body quantum systems initialized in different thermal states and examine when the initially farther state relaxes to the (non-equilibrium) steady state faster. We claim that the number of conserved quantities in the unitary part plays a crucial role: the Mpemba effect is possible only when the Hamiltonian commutes with other extensive operators or is integrable. The reason lies in the dynamical evolution happening in spaces of different dimensions. When energy is the only approximately conserved quantity, dissipation pushes the dynamics within a single-parameter manifold of different thermal states. In contrast, for Hamiltonians with several conserved quantities, the dynamics drift in the multi-dimensional space of generalized Gibbs ensembles, whose distance to the steady state is less trivial. We provide numerical results for large system sizes using tensor networks and free-fermion techniques, thereby supporting our claim.

record.abstract: How does evolutionary information become structural knowledge? AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with remarkable accuracy, yet how it transforms comparative sequence information into three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. Here, we use mechanistic interpretability to follow this transformation through AlphaFold 3 and identify a computational principle underlying its structural inference. By extracting single- and pair-representations across the model's forward pass and combining representational-geometry analysis, linear probing, activation patching, and perturbation of the multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and its phylogenetic diversity, we show that AlphaFold 3 does not simply infer structure from raw sequence nor from MSA depth. Instead, a small number of sufficiently divergent homologues provides enough comparative information to largely recover the structure predicted using the full MSA. The pairformer transforms this evolutionary signal into a compact latent space in which residue-pair distances, contacts, fold similarity, and structural confidence become progressively decodable. Removing the MSA disrupts these latent geometries. Replacing it with evolutionarily similar homologues provides substantially less information, while evolutionarily unrelated sequences fail to rescue prediction despite preserving the formal alignment input. In contrast, phylogenetically diverse MSA subsampling largely restores both prediction accuracy and representational coherence. These results suggest that AlphaFold 3 has learned to infer structure by constraining its geometric priors and structural hypotheses by the sequence variation of the MSA. This framework helps explain both the model's remarkable predictive power and its characteristic failure modes, with direct implications for protein design, conformational diversity, out-of-distribution generalization, and the interpretation of model confidence.

record.abstract: To track state of health (SOH), second-life potential and design warranties, it is necessary to accurately characterise lithium-ion battery capacity degradation. This paper compares the methodological approaches used for regression models of capacity fade, using synthetic degradation curves which are built from the structure of the publicly available Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1 (OBDD1) of eight 740 mAh cells discharged using an ARTEMIS urban drive-cycle at 40 °C, with each degradation profile sampled every 100 cycles. The quantitative results provided are thus illustrative, whereas the qualitative conclusions made on the problem of model selection are robust and extend to the real data. Linear, quadratic and cubic polynomials are compared to describe the capacity-versus-cycle trajectory and compared to Gaussian process regression (GPR) for prediction of end of life (EOL, 80% SOH). The quadratic model fits the dominant fade (R² ≈ 0.97), the cubic model improves the fit with the “knee” in the later life of the battery (R² ≈ 0.99), and GPR has the lowest point error (RMSE ≈ 2 mAh), but the gain over the cubic polynomial is low in absolute terms (about 0.3% of nominal capacity), and GPR's primary benefit is the well-calibrated uncertainty rather than point accuracy. From the early-life extrapolation experiment, it can be observed that the remaining useful life is consistently overestimated by low-order polynomials and thus the motivation of using uncertainty-aware approaches. The entire pipeline is made available as reproducible code, to enable direct substitution of real measurements.

record.abstract: Learning and optimal control under robust Markov decision processes (MDPs) have received increasing attention, yet most existing theory, algorithms, and applications focus on finite-horizon or discounted models. Long-run average-reward formulations, while natural in many operations research and management contexts, remain underexplored. This is primarily because the dynamic programming foundations are technically challenging and only partially understood, with several fundamental questions remaining open. This paper steps toward a general framework for average-reward robust MDPs by analyzing the constant-gain setting. We study the average-reward robust control problem with possible information asymmetries between the controller and an S-rectangular adversary. record.abstract: The advent of multiple neuroimaging methodologies has greatly aided in the conceptualization of large-scale functional brain networks in the field of cognitive neuroscience. Here we improve the accessibility of a previously developed whole-brain template of canonical functional brain networks, expanding it into a powerful atlas, by manually labeling, organizing, and describing these networks with terms familiar to the fields of cognitive and affective neuroscience. These data-driven functional networks were developed by utilizing more than 100,000 resting-state fMRI datasets and are highly replicable across individual subjects and datasets and capture information from multiple spatial scales. The benefits of this atlas are not limited to future template-based or reference-guided analyses, but also extend to other data-driven neuroimaging approaches across modalities, such as those using blind independent component analysis (ICA). Future studies utilizing this atlas will contribute to greater harmonization and standardization in functional neuroimaging research.

record.abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

record.abstract: Abstract High-energy nuclear physics explores the properties of strongly interacting matter created in relativistic collisions of nuclei. Femtoscopy, a subfield of high-energy physics, utilizes quantum-statistical correlations of particles to characterize the space-time geometry of the particle-emitting source. Recent measurements and phenomenological investigations indicated that the shape of the source for identical pions can be well-described by Lévy-stable distributions. The significant power-law tail of the pion source observed both in experiment and in simulations has been shown to originate from the process of Lévy walk during the hadronic scattering phase of the collisions. To better understand the physical processes behind the formation of such power laws, an important next step is to investigate particle species dependence, especially the source shape of identical kaon and proton pairs. As a direct continuation of our previous studies, in this paper, we present a detailed three-dimensional investigation of the two-particle source shape in simulations of Au + Au collisions at 200 GeV per nucleon pair collision energy using the EPOS3 model. We show the dependence of the extracted femtoscopic source parameters on particle species, centrality and average transverse mass. We find that the scale parameters do not show a clear transverse mass scaling between particle species, as there are systematic differences in the overlapping regions. The power-law exponents of pion and kaon pairs are compatible, while for protons it is higher, closer to the Gaussian limit. When new experimental measurements of kaon and proton correlations become available, these results will provide the basis of a data-model comparison.

record.abstract: Deep learning (DL) has achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation by learning data-driven representations from large-scale annotated datasets. However, medical images are often collected independently across clinical sites, resulting in substantial domain shifts due to differences in imaging modalities, acquisition protocols, and intensity distributions. Meanwhile, segmentation classes may vary across sites due to differences in annotation standards, leading to class shifts. These evolving domains and class definitions can substantially degrade segmentation performance on newly encountered data, while sequential adaptation may cause catastrophic forgetting of knowledge acquired from previously encountered domains and classes. Existing incremental learning methods for medical image segmentation primarily address either domain shifts or class shifts, with these two settings largely investigated independently. This separation leaves a critical gap in developing a unified approach that can simultaneously adapt to evolving domains and newly introduced classes while retaining previously acquired knowledge. To address this challenge, we propose Fisher-Guided Continuously Adaptive Representation Learning, a unified framework for domain- and class-incremental 3D volumetric medical image segmentation. FGCARL comprises two key components: Mutual Adaptive Instance Representation (MAIR), which adaptively aligns feature distributions across sequentially encountered domains through bidirectional normalization and denormalization, and Fisher-Guided Knowledge Retention (FGKR), which selectively preserves parameters important for previously learned domains and classes through Fisher-guided regularization. Experimental results demonstrate that FGCARL consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods, effectively adapting to domain and class shifts while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

record.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly pervasive and powerful, the ability to audit AI-based systems is growing in importance. However, explainability for artificial intelligence systems is not a one-size-fits-all solution; different target audiences have varying requirements and expectations for explanations. While various approaches to explainability have been proposed, most explainable artificial intelligence methods for tabular data focus on explaining the outputs of supervised machine learning models using the input features. However, a user's ability to understand an explanation depends on their understanding of such features. Therefore, it is in the best interest of the system designer to try to pre-select understandable features for producing a global explanation of an ML model. Unfortunately, no measure currently exists to assess the degree to which a user understands a given input feature. This work introduces two psychometrically validated scales that quantitatively seek to assess users' perceived understanding of tabular input features for supervised classification problems. Specifically, these scales, one for numerical and one for categorical data, each with two factors and comprising 8 and 9 items, aim to assign a score to each input feature, effectively producing a rank and allowing for the quantification of feature prioritisation. A confirmatory factor analysis demonstrates a strong relationship between such items and a good fit of the two-factor structure for each scale. This research presents a novel method for assessing understanding and outlines potential applications in the domain of explainable artificial intelligence.

record.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported telemedicine may extend clinical expertise to rural communities, yet its benefits can be offset by unequal connectivity, digital literacy, data representation, and institutional readiness. This study examined the efficacy and health-equity implications of AI-powered telemedicine in post-pandemic rural Indonesia. A qualitative-dominant, convergent mixed-methods secondary study integrated reflexive thematic analysis of peer-reviewed qualitative evidence and Indonesian policy documents with descriptive synthesis of verified national and clinical datasets. Evidence included 2023 national internet statistics, a 63,012-person chronic-disease survey, a 311-patient rheumatology survey, and a 15-interview qualitative study. Telemedicine was most effective for stable follow-up, medication management, specialist access, and travel-cost avoidance, but was less reliable for first diagnosis, unstable disease, and examination-dependent care. Rural internet use (59.33%) remained 17.47 percentage points below urban use (76.80%). Among people with hypertension and/or diabetes, 98.0% reported no telemedicine use, indicating a substantial implementation gap. Four integrated themes emerged: conditional clinical efficacy, redistributed rather than eliminated access burdens, algorithmic amplification of structural disadvantage, and the necessity of human-mediated hybrid care. Conclusion: AI-powered telemedicine is neither inherently equalizing nor intrinsically exclusionary. Its equity effect depends on assisted access, low-bandwidth design, representative validation, clinician oversight, interoperability, and disaggregated monitoring.

record.abstract: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. For models such as Ouro that keep a separate key-value (KV) cache per loop, cache memory limits the batch size that amortizes repeated weight reads. Uniform-bit quantization and fixed rules per loop do not allocate precision according to each layer's sensitivity in each loop. Measurements on Ouro show that quantization sensitivity varies across (loop, layer) cells, and the sum of individual cell damages approximates the overall output damage. Sharing damage also varies by cell, with later loops generally tolerating sharing better. Skipping low-attention values to save reads produces errors that compound across loops. LoopKV uses a one-time offline profile to choose 4-bit storage, 2-bit storage or reuse of the final loop's KV for each cell. The planner minimizes reads under budgets for predicted damage and storage. record.abstract: Multireference calculations on transition-metal complexes, on classical or quantum hardware, depend on the choice of active space. record.abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

record.abstract: Gravitational-wave data is never analysed without some conditioning: filtering and tapering act multiplicatively on the noise, destroying the stationarity on which the Whittle likelihood --- the backbone of nearly all gravitational-wave inference --- rests. We provide an analytical and numerical framework to assess the impact of noise mis-modelling when signal and noise parameters are inferred jointly in the presence of gaps. From a Fisher-matrix formalism verified against Bayesian inference, we obtain closed forms for the model uncertainties, their maximum-likelihood estimates and the true scatter in the latter, for various approximations to the likelihood. The Fisher-based linear formalism is extended through the Godambe--White curvature to the non-linear regime that severe mis-modelling produces. We survey gap families from long, well-tapered interruptions to short, high-rate ones, injecting massive black-hole binaries. Except in the case of frequent gaps, we show that the windowed covariance is well approximated by its leading diagonal --- the window convolved with the power spectral density --- for the estimation of both signal and noise parameters. By omitting the convolution, the signal sector remains unbiased but the noise parameters, in particular the optical-metrology noise which is dominant at high frequency, is displaced by over an order of magnitude in power. At the highest glitch rates the diagonal approximation stays accurate yet loses an order of magnitude in precision. To remedy this, we propose an exact time-domain likelihood of the surviving samples which can be efficiently (and accurately solved) via preconditioned conjugate gradient methods.

Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, the pipeline produces 11,445 calibrated diffraction curves, released in the open database COF-PEAK. Compared with a hand digitization of 60 panels, extracted peak positions differ by a median of only 0.07 degrees. Whereas papers usually report only a few peak angles, which limits further analysis, the digitized curves enable tracking how peak prominence, a possible marker of crystallinity, changes with synthesis conditions. Vision LLMs and classical CV can thus turn such figures into reusable experimental data.

record.abstract: We study extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) evolving in a scalar cloud environment that may form through superradiant instabilities, using a fully relativistic perturbative framework that allows for eccentric and inclined orbits. EMRIs, consisting of a stellar-mass compact object inspiraling into a supermassive black hole, are key sources for space-based gravitational-wave detectors such as LISA. Previous relativistic studies of EMRIs in scalar clouds have been restricted to circular, equatorial motion. Here, instead, we focus on a Schwarzschild black hole background to incorporate eccentricity and orbital inclination. By computing the scalar energy and angular momentum scattered off to spatial infinity and absorbed at the event horizon, we show that orbital eccentricity can induce a dense spectrum of resonances near the last stable orbit, associated with strong relativistic apsidal precession. We further find that orbital inclination can significantly modify the orbital energy and angular momentum losses. In particular, we identify a critical inclination angle below which, at sufficiently small orbital radii, there is a net transfer of energy from the scalar cloud to the orbit. Moreover, for sufficiently large eccentricities, resonances associated with relativistic apsidal precession persist across the full range of inclinations, although their structure changes significantly between prograde and retrograde orbits. These results provide a foundation for future studies of EMRIs in scalar cloud environments on fully generic orbits around spinning black holes.

record.abstract: Abstract Line intensity mapping (LIM) is a novel observational technique in astrophysics that utilizes the integrated emission from multiple atomic and molecular transition lines from galaxies to probe the complex physics of galaxy formation and evolution, as well as the large-scale structure of the Universe. Modeling multiple line luminosities of galaxies with varying masses or their host halo masses poses significant uncertainty due to the lack of observational data across a wide redshift range and the intricate nature of astrophysical processes, making them challenging to model analytically or in simulations. While future experiments aim to measure multiple line intensities up to z ∼ 8 across a wide volume using tomographic methods, we leverage publicly available datasets from the cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiment Planck and the galaxy survey eBOSS to constrain the CO(3–2) emission from galaxies. We stack galaxies on the Planck CO(2–1) map and measure galaxy-correlated emission at z ∼ 0.5. Its interpretation as CO(3–2) depends on the continuum model, spectral response, and background treatment, which turns into the signal detection confidence between 2.2 σ and 3.4 σ . Our findings demonstrate that stacking methods are already viable with existing observations from CMB experiments and galaxy surveys, and are complementary to traditional LIM experiments.

record.abstract: The resolution of conventional imaging is fundamentally constrained by the diffraction limit. Here we demonstrate that this limit can be overcome using classical thermal light, through the correlation of multiphoton subsystems. By resolving the photon numbers detected in the two arms of a Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer, the correlation function exhibits a narrowed peak or dip whose width is tunable via the average photon number. Temporal and spatial super-resolution enhancements up to 11.8-fold and 5.1-fold, respectively, are experimentally achieved. As a proof-of-principle experiment, a double-pinhole that is completely unresolved by standard ghost imaging becomes clearly distinguishable via the correlation of two-photon versus zero-photon. The principle of this super-resolution imaging can be interpreted as a combination of classical super-resolution imaging and quantum super-resolution imaging. This work provides a versatile platform for super-resolution imaging and lithography, and opens a new avenue for exploring the boundary between classical and nonclassical phenomena.

record.abstract: High-fidelity simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains requires physical wall boundary treatment and geometric representation compatible with high-order reconstruction, since viscous shear stresses and conductive heat fluxes are concentrated in a thin near-wall region. Conventional high-order methods often suffer from loss of accuracy near curved walls or require complicated wall treatments. To address these issues, in this paper, we develop a NURBS-enhanced $k$-exact finite-volume method for the steady compressible Navier--Stokes equations on hybrid meshes. To incorporate physical wall conditions into the high-order discretization, we develop a wall boundary treatment that employs sequential reconstruction without requiring the reconstruction variables to coincide with those used to prescribe the boundary conditions. The NURBS-based boundary representation is used to obtain a high-order accurate description of curved boundaries, and the diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux is employed to enhance numerical robustness. A variety of numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

record.abstract: When applied to two-dimensional features such as images, Mamba-based methods either flatten the feature map into 1D sequences and fuse multiple scans, which breaks spatial adjacency and multiplies computation, or recurse directly on the 2D grid but rescale the recurrence with a fixed input-independent factor and aggregate only the predecessors on a single anti-diagonal, leaving the discrete step unconstrained by 2D stability theory. We propose \textbf{FM-Mamba}, a native 2D selective state space model built on the general Fornasini--Marchesini (FM) model. Its coupled recurrence evolves along both spatial axes; cross-axis coupling induces a discrete diagonal-predecessor term $\tilde A_0$, and two independent input-dependent step sizes $Δ_1(i,j)$, $Δ_2(i,j)$ govern propagation along the two axes, so that the coefficients adapt per position and per direction. A normalized ratio $r_k=a_{0,k}/(a_{1,k}a_{2,k})$ yields a closed-form piecewise bound on the two step sizes; when a configuration falls outside the stable interval the steps are projected onto this bound, and the criterion is re-verified per position after training, which suppresses systematic local amplification without global damping. The recurrence is executed by a dual-diagonal wavefront scan: each update gathers information from two anti-diagonals, and the input enters the current state through a single projection, so that neither training nor inference flattens the feature map. Code is available at https://github.com/BitSsm/FM-Mamba-Runtime

record.abstract: Abstract JWST has revealed a substantial population of “Little Red Dots” (LRDs) at z > 4, challenging conventional active galactic muclei (AGN) frameworks. However, the low-redshift regime remains largely unexplored. In the second paper of the (LRDs) 2 series, we present a systematic selection from DESI DR1 and identify 27 LRDs at z = 0.2–0.9, yielding a number density lower limit of 7.5 × 10 −10 cMpc −3 . We conducted near-IR spectroscopic follow-up observations for 21 of them, revealing their full spectral energy distribution (SED) shapes and emission lines. These low- z LRDs share the hallmark properties of their high- z counterparts: compact morphology, V-shaped UV-optical continua, broad Balmer emission with extreme decrements (median H α /H β ∼ 15), frequent Balmer absorption (70%), and blackbody-like optical-to-near-IR continua. All have low metallicity, occupy the same regions in the BPT diagram as high- z LRDs, and have softer ionizing spectra than typical AGNs. The consistency between low- z and high- z LRD properties indicates the same physical processes at work. The correlation between broad-line Balmer luminosity and L 5100 deviates from that of local type-1 AGNs, limiting the direct application of local BH mass calibrations. Ionized [O iii ] outflows are ubiquitous (78%). One LRD at z = 0.196, J1717+3807, shows robust long-term variability in the i and Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) bands. The optical-to-near-IR continua of LRDs reveal a wide range of temperatures ∼2000–4700 K (peak 0.6–1.4 μ m), with a subset showing cooler and larger envelopes than those at high z . Low- z LRDs serve not only as proximate laboratories for probing the nature of LRDs, but also trace the cosmic evolution of this population from the cosmic dawn to the present day.

record.abstract: The integration of advanced materials and intelligent technologies is transforming sustainable engineering by enabling resource-efficient manufacturing, adaptive systems, real-time monitoring, and improved human–machine interaction. Conventional engineering approaches often rely on resource-intensive materials, energy-consuming processes, and limited monitoring capabilities, creating environmental and operational challenges throughout product life cycles. Advanced materials, including conductive polymers, nanofibers, stimuli-responsive polymers, shape-memory materials, photovoltaic fibers, and flexible electronic structures, offer opportunities to address these challenges through multifunctionality, lightweight design, and improved system adaptability. Concurrently, intelligent technologies, such as embedded sensors, digital monitoring systems, data-driven decision support, and connected wearable devices, support more efficient resource utilization and condition-based operation. Smart textiles provide a particularly relevant example because they combine material innovation with sensing, communication, energy harvesting, and user-oriented functionality. Applications in healthcare, industrial safety, energy management, environmental monitoring, and engineering education demonstrate the interdisciplinary potential of these technologies. However, their sustainable implementation requires careful consideration of material toxicity, manufacturing energy, durability, washability, electronic waste, recyclability, data privacy, and economic accessibility. This paper presents a literature-based technical review of advanced materials and intelligent technologies for sustainable engineering applications. It examines material characteristics, technological integration, application domains, environmental considerations, and implementation barriers. It also discusses life-cycle assessment, circular product design, sustainability-oriented engineering education, and challenge-based learning as complementary strategies for responsible innovation. The review indicates that technological performance alone is insufficient to establish sustainability; environmental integrity, human well-being, economic feasibility, and end-of-life management must be considered together. An integrated framework combining sustainable material selection, intelligent system design, lifecycle evaluation, and interdisciplinary education is proposed to guide future research and engineering practice.

record.abstract: Impedance mismatch remains one of the most consequential yet systematically underestimated sources of performance degradation in wireless communication systems. When source and load impedances at any interface in a radio frequency chain fail to achieve conjugate matching, a portion of the signal power is reflected rather than transferred, producing quantifiable losses in transmit efficiency, receiver sensitivity, noise figure, gain linearity, and overall link margin. The challenge is compounded in modern wireless prototype development by the absence of a unified engineering workflow that translates component-level impedance measurements into actionable system-level performance predictions. Engineers routinely characterize individual components on a vector network analyzer (VNA) and construct link budgets using idealized datasheet specifications, but the gap between these two activities means that accumulated mismatch losses across the full signal chain frequently escape notice until receiver sensitivity or range tests reveal unexplained shortfalls during board bring-up. This paper addresses that gap by presenting a comprehensive modeling framework that quantifies impedance mismatch impact at each interface of a wireless RF front-end, including the power amplifier output, low-noise amplifier input, antenna feed point, RF switch transitions, and inter-stage transmission lines, and propagates these contributions through a modified Friis cascade chain into a unified link budget model. The framework draws on VNA S-parameter measurements, Smith chart analysis, Advanced Design System (ADS) simulation, load-pull characterization, and Y-factor noise figure measurement to construct per-interface mismatch profiles. The profiles are then processed through a four-stage pipeline: interface mismatch characterization, per-stage performance penalty computation, cascaded chain analysis, and link budget integration with sensitivity ranking. The framework is validated through application to a Bluetooth 5.0 short-range wireless prototype, where it accurately predicted a 3.2 dB receiver sensitivity shortfall attributable to antenna-to-LNA interface mismatch and guided a two-iteration matching network correction that restored the sensitivity to within 0.1 dB of the design target. The methodology is directly applicable to IoT platform bring-up, where compact antenna geometries and tight power budgets make impedance non-idealities particularly costly.

The study aims to depict the optimised parameter values at which enhanced thermal conductivity of nanofluids results in more efficient cooling. To achieve this, mixed convection nanofluid (Cu-water) flow over a shrinking sheet under radiative effects is investigated numerically using finite element method (FEM). The analysis incorporates key parameters such as the suction, thermal conductivity, radiation and mixed convection which govern the flow and heat transfer characteristics. The numerical investigation depicts that suction is the most dominant factor which helps to reduce the boundary layer thickness and enhance heat transfer. The mixed convection parameter also contributes to higher heat transfer rate, simultaneously increasing the skin friction. Corresponding diagrams are plotted to illustrate the outcomes. Also, results obtained statistically by Response Surface Methodology (RSM) using MATLAB® are investigated for optimised value of parameters. The results from the RSM model show a strong positive correlation with our numerical FEM results. The RSM-ANOVA optimisation reveals a strong correlation, giving accuracy of 0.975, highlighting the roles of suction and radiative heat transfer in determining thermal behaviour. record.abstract: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.

record.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a simple yet effective continuous tabular data watermarking mechanism with statistical guarantees. We show theoretically that the proposed watermark can be effectively detected, while faithfully preserving the data fidelity. The general idea of the watermarking mechanism is to achieve the watermarking through a strategic embedding based on simple data binning. Specifically, it divides the feature’s value range into finely segmented intervals and embeds watermarks into selected “green list" intervals. To detect the watermarks, we develop a principled statistical hypothesis-testing framework with minimal assumptions: it remains valid as long as the underlying data distribution has a continuous density function. Furthermore, we demonstrate robustness of the proposed watermarking mechanism against various attacks. The watermarking efficacy is demonstrated through rigorous theoretical analysis and empirical validation, highlighting its utility in enhancing the security of synthetic and real-world datasets with continuous tabular features.

record.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides certified backward reachable tubes (BRTs) for safety-critical robotic systems, but the level-set computation scales exponentially in the state dimension and has historically been performed offline. We present a CUDA implementation of the canonical WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichs level-set Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs solver for 2D, 3D, and 4D dynamics that is fast enough to run inside a robot's control loop. record.abstract: The Boltzmann transport equation describes particle transport across collisional regimes, but resolving its velocity dependence is expensive. Moment methods reduce this cost by evolving finitely many velocity moments, requiring a closure for unresolved higher-order moments. Data-driven closures can represent these moments accurately, yet without structural constraints they may produce complex characteristic speeds and unstable simulations. Learned Boltzmann closures with guaranteed hyperbolicity have so far been formulated in one spatial dimension; in multiple dimensions, hyperbolicity must hold in every direction simultaneously. We develop, to the best of our knowledge, the first data-driven closure for multidimensional Hermite moment systems of the linear Boltzmann equation that is hyperbolic by construction. The network learns a symmetric positive-definite symmetrizer shared by all spatial directions and restricted to a subspace that preserves the known lower-order transport equations; the unresolved rows follow from a symmetric completion. Every directional Jacobian thus has real eigenvalues and a complete set of eigenvectors for every network output and at any truncation order. The closure is trained only on spatial derivatives of unresolved moments from kinetic reference solutions, with no solver in the training loop, and evolved by a partially conservative discontinuous Galerkin method. In two-dimensional experiments in the transition and scattering-dominated regimes, a single learned third-order system with ten moments remains stable in all cases. Averaged over time, it is more accurate than the classical P7 and P15 truncations with 36 and 136 moments in every experiment, and its density error is about two orders of magnitude smaller than that of the P3 truncation with the same moments.

record.abstract: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. record.abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.

record.abstract: Altermagnetic order gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting of electronic and magnonic excitations even in the absence of a net magnetization. Here, we investigate the magnetic field dependence of the spin-wave spectrum of altermagnetic $α$-MnTe using inelastic neutron scattering and linear spin-wave theory. An in-plane magnetic field continuously reorients the Néel vector by overcoming the weak crystalline anisotropy, while remaining small compared with the dominant exchange scale. We find that this reorientation leaves the magnon energies and line widths essentially unchanged, but strongly modifies the measured spectral intensity through the transverse-momentum projection. Our results demonstrate a clear separation between the soft orientational degree of freedom of the antiferromagnetic order and the robust exchange-dominated chiral magnon spectrum. This combination establishes $α$-MnTe as a platform for reconfigurable magnon coupling, in which external fields tune how excitations interact with polarized probes without substantially altering their frequency or coherence.

record.abstract: Abstract We discuss the excitons in flat band systems. Quantum metric plays a central role in determining the properties of single exciton excitations as well as the exciton condensate. While the electrons and holes are supposed to be extremely heavy in flat bands, the excitons (the bound state of an electron-hole pair) could be light and mobile. In particular, we show that the inverse of the effective mass tensor of excitons is proportional to the quantum metric tensor. Meanwhile, the flat band excitons have a finite size, lower bounded by the trace of the quantum metric tensor. Given the properties of single exciton excitation, one can argue for the formation of exciton condensate. Because of the quantum metric, the exciton condensate can support dissipationless counterflow supercurrent, implying the stability of exciton condensate.

record.abstract: Accurate copying of nucleic acid sequences is essential for self-replicating systems. Modern cells achieve error ratios as low as 10-9 with sophisticated enzymes capable of kinetic proofreading. In contrast, experiments probing enzyme-free copying of RNA and DNA as potential prebiotic replication processes find error ratios on the order of 10%. Given this low intrinsic copying fidelity, plausible scenarios for the spontaneous emergence of molecular evolution require an accuracy-enhancing mechanism. Here, we study a 'kinetic error filtering' scenario that dramatically boosts the likelihood of producing exact copies of nucleic acid sequences. The mechanism exploits the observation that initial errors in template-directed polymerization of both DNA and RNA are likely to trigger a cascade of consecutive errors and significantly stall downstream extension. We incorporate these characteristics into a mathematical model with experimentally estimated parameters, and leverage this model to probe to what extent accurate and faulty polymerization products can be kinetically discriminated. Limiting the time window for polymerization prevents completion of erroneous strands, resulting in a pool in which full-length products show an enhanced accuracy. This comes at the price of a concomitant reduction in yield. However, the yield rate and the fidelity can be simultaneously increased by kinetic error filtering, if the templates are not too long. Within cyclically varying environments, e.g., temperature cycles in hydrothermal systems, repeated copying attempts could produce exact copies of sequences as long as 50mers within their lifetime, facilitating the emergence and maintenance of catalytically active oligonucleotides.

record.abstract: We show analytically that the convergence of the QNM expansion of the retarded Green's function of the Schwarzschild spacetime is set by a singularity in the complex time plane. The singularity has a simple geometric origin: it is an example of a `bouncing singularity' in the language of AdS/CFT literature, caused by a null geodesic which bounces from the black hole singularity. Our work explains why the QNM convergence region at real times is bounded by null ray which scatters from the gravitational potential at a seemingly unremarkable point ($r_* = 0$ in the conventions of previous work) -- this ray is the same distance from the origin as the bouncing singularity in the relevant complex plane. The same set of singularities are responsible for an annular region of convergence for the Matsubara mode sum which describes the early time behaviour of the Schwarzschild Green's function for perturbations close to the horizon.

record.abstract: Abstract A notable achievement of the first generation of JWST surveys was the discovery of an abundance of faint high-redshift (z > 4) broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the Lbol < 1045 erg s−1 regime, previously only accessible at z < 1. The high prevalence of absorption features in their broad hydrogen lines is one of the peculiarities of a significant fraction of this new population. In this paper, we conduct a broad census of Balmer absorption in a sample of 47 Type-1 AGN spanning 2 < z < 7. Accounting for incompleteness of JWST spectroscopic data, we estimate that $44_{-6}^{+21}$ % of Little Red Dots (LRDs) have absorption in Hα while the incidence rate is <25 % (at 2σ) in Little Blue Dots (LBDs). Additionally, R1000 JWST/NIRSpec data is strongly resolution limited, implying an inability to disentangle Doppler broadening in the absorption from optical depth effects. This is alleviated with R2700 observations, although some degeneracies remain. We find a significant correlation between the velocity of the Balmer absorption and the [OIII]5007 narrow line luminosity, suggesting a common driving mechanism. We do not find any other significant correlations (and do not confirm previously claimed correlations) between Balmer absorption and other spectral properties of LRDs (except for the expected correlation between Hα and Hβ absorption velocities). Comparing LRDs, quasars and stellar Hα absorbers, we establish that absorption in both LRDs and broad absorption line quasars is consistent with radiatively driven outflows, echoing the physics of variable stars yet occurring at vastly different scales.
